title: Stake Engine documentation reference
purpose: Local working reference for creating a Stake Engine game. This is a distilled engineering summary with source links, not a replacement for the publisher's current documentation or contractual terms.

core_model.platform: Stake Engine uses the Carrot Remote Gaming Server (RGS) to host and run provider games.
sdk_parts: Math SDK: Python-based game rules, simulations, optimization, analysis, and publication-file generation.
Frontend SDK: PixiJS/Svelte-based browser game rendering and interaction layer.
RGS integration: session, wallet, round, and event APIs used by the frontend.
core_model.publication_constraint: Published games use static files. Game outcomes are precomputed into game books/events and lookup tables; a weighted lookup selects a simulation and the RGS returns its events through the play flow.
core_model.important_implication: The frontend displays events produced by math output. It should not independently invent outcomes that are absent from the event payload.

recommended_build_order: Choose the game mechanic and target math profile (RTP, volatility, hit rate, max win, modes).
Set up the Math SDK and start from the closest sample/template game.
Implement game configuration, state, calculations, win logic, and events.
Run simulations, analysis, optimization, and format checks.
Inspect the generated books, lookup tables, indexes, and publish files.
Create the frontend app from a matching sample and render every emitted event.
Integrate the RGS wallet flow and resume in-progress rounds correctly.
Test locally in Storybook/dev mode, then package and submit through the applicable Engine workflow.

setup.rust_cargo: Required only when using the optimization algorithm
setup.windows_note: The docs note that Windows uses python rather than python3 and provides a Windows virtual-environment activation example.

directory_roles.games: Game-specific configuration, calculations, executables, and run scripts.
directory_roles.src/calculations: Reusable board, symbol, and win calculations.
directory_roles.src/config: Configuration generation for RGS, frontend, and optimizer.
directory_roles.src/events: Event data structures shared with the frontend.
directory_roles.src/write_data: Simulation output, compression, and force files.
directory_roles.utils: Analysis, analytics, LUT tools, decompression, format checks, and helpers.

math_sdk.game_state: GameState configuration commonly distinguishes basegame and freegame because rules, triggers, multipliers, and win-level handling can differ by game type.

events.role: Events are JSON snapshots returned by the play API and contain everything the frontend needs to display the round.

shape.other_fields: game-specific values such as board, wins, counters, multipliers, or special actions

rules: Append events to the book in sequence.
Emit an event whenever new player-visible state needs to be communicated.
Frontend must handle every event type emitted by the math output.
Win amounts are represented in the SDK event conventions; follow the current SDK types/examples rather than guessing units.

output_model.lookup_table: CSV summary mapping simulation number to selection weight/probability and payout multiplier.
output_model.book: Compressed/static game logic and event data indexed by simulation.
output_model.index: Publication index required by the RGS file format.
output_model.analysis: Can produce RTP, hit-rate, win-distribution, and PAR-style statistics from lookup tables, force files, paytables, and events.
output_model.quick_start_example: A sample run can generate files under library/publish_files and can be run with a small number of uncompressed results for inspection.

monorepo_shape.packages: Shared config, constants, state, fetchers, slot utilities, audio, event emitters, XState, Pixi/Svelte components, and UI packages.
monorepo_shape.entry_pattern: Each app has a SvelteKit route and a Game component. Context must be initialized before rendering components that consume shared game context.

frontend_sdk.integration_principle: Use the generated math events as the source of truth and make the frontend animation/state machine consume them in order.

rgs.initialization: Call POST /wallet/authenticate with sessionID before any other wallet endpoint.
basic_flow: Call /wallet/play with sessionID, amount, and mode.
Call /wallet/end-round after the round is complete.

endpoints./wallet/authenticate: Validates the session and returns balance, currency, bet configuration, jurisdiction, and active/last round information.
endpoints./wallet/play: Starts a round and debits the bet amount.
endpoints./wallet/end-round: Completes the round and triggers payout.
endpoints./bet/event: Stores an in-progress game event so a round can be resumed after disconnect/reload.

rgs.resume_behavior: If authenticate returns an active round, use its round.event state to resume the correct animation/game position.
rgs.url_rule: Do not hardcode rgs_url; read it from the game URL/query context.

money_and_bets.precision: Engine monetary values are integers with six decimal places of precision; 1,000,000 represents 1.00 unit.
bet_rules: Bet must be between minBet and maxBet returned by authenticate.
Bet must be divisible by stepBet.
Use returned betLevels to guide the UI.
money_and_bets.minimum_bet_guidance: New games should support small denominations such as 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, and 0.10 USD-equivalent levels where the game design permits.
money_and_bets.currencies: The docs describe fiat currencies plus social-casino currencies XGC, XSC, and XEC. Currency affects display; game logic uses the integer amount convention.

distribution.choice: At first submission choose Only on Stake or Stake and the Engine Network.
notes: Distribution choice is separate from the payment model.
Network distribution can use the whole network or selected operators.
Network games have different revenue shares and Stake promotion/placement conditions.

project_checklist: Define original game concept and jurisdiction/compliance assumptions.
Select a sample game/template and confirm the SDK/repository version.
Define paytable, bet levels, target RTP, volatility, hit rate, feature triggers, and max win.
Implement deterministic event/state structures before polishing visuals.
Generate and inspect static books, lookup tables, indexes, and compressed files.
Run statistical analysis and format verification.
Implement all RGS error, loading, reconnect, and active-round states.
Test desktop/mobile and supported languages from the query parameters.
Review current submission, licensing, distribution, and payment terms before launch.
maintenance_note: Re-check the source pages before implementation or submission because SDK versions, API schemas, supported currencies, submission rules, and commercial terms can change.
